test_title: PYST 60: SSC CGL 2024 - Quantitative Aptitude (Held On 13 Sept, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: maths
question: 2 biscuits and 1 chocolate cost ₹69. 2 chocolates and 3 cups of coffee cost ₹127. 3 biscuits, 4 chocolates and 2 cups of coffee cost ₹229. Find the total cost (in ₹) of 5 biscuits, 5 chocolates and 5 cups of coffee.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let b, c, and f be the unit prices of biscuit, chocolate, and coffee.

Given: 2b + c = 69; 2c + 3f = 127; 3b + 4c + 2f = 229.

From the first, c = 69 − 2b. Substitute this in the other two equations:

4b − 3f = 11 and 5b − 2f = 47. Solving these gives b = 17, f = 19.

Hence, c = 69 − 2(17) = 35. Total cost of 1 set = 17 + 35 + 19 = 71.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹355.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Let the cost of 1 biscuit, 1 chocolate, and 1 coffee be b, c, and f respectively.

Given:

⇒ 2b + c = 69 --- (1)

⇒ 2c + 3f = 127 --- (2)

⇒ 3b + 4c + 2f = 229 --- (3)

From (1), we get c = 69 − 2b.

Substitute c in (2):

⇒ 2(69 − 2b) + 3f = 127

⇒ 138 − 4b + 3f = 127

⇒ 4b − 3f = 11 --- (4)

Substitute c in (3):

⇒ 3b + 4(69 − 2b) + 2f = 229

⇒ 3b + 276 − 8b + 2f = 229

⇒ 5b − 2f = 47 --- (5)

Multiply (4) by 2 and (5) by 3:

⇒ 8b − 6f = 22

⇒ 15b − 6f = 141

Subtracting the first equation from the second:

⇒ 7b = 119 ⇒ b = 17

Putting b = 17 in (1):

⇒ 2(17) + c = 69 ⇒ c = 69 − 34 = 35

Putting c = 35 in (2):

⇒ 2(35) + 3f = 127 ⇒ 3f = 127 − 70 = 57 ⇒ f = 19

Total cost of 5 of each item = 5 × (b + c + f)

⇒ 5 × (17 + 35 + 19) = 5 × 71 = 355

**∴ The correct answer is ₹355.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

System of Linear Equations

A collection of one or more linear equations involving the same variables. They can be solved systematically using substitution, elimination, or matrix methods to find the unique solution values.

Substitution Method

A method for solving systems of equations by expressing one variable in terms of the others and substituting it into the remaining equations to reduce the number of variables.

Elimination Method

A process of multiplying equations by specific constants so that adding or subtracting them eliminates one of the variables entirely, allowing for easier resolution.
